full_judgment:
2. In this application, the legality of the Order dated 15-3-2001, passed by the Artha Rin Court, Comilla, in Artha Execution Case No.339 of 2004, rejecting the prayer for amendment of an earlier petition for compromise (solenama) (Annexure-D), has been challenged. 

 4. Thereafter, the decree holder and judgment debtors both jointly filed an application on 5-6-2006 under section 38 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (the 'Act') in three execution cases, namely, Artha Rin Execution Case Nos. 337 of 2004, 338 of 2004 and 339 of 2004 arising out of 3 separate Artha Rin suits, namely, Artha Rin Suit Nos. 39 of 1995, 67 of 1995 and 66 of 1995, respectively (Annexure-B). It is stated in the said petition that in pursuance of an earlier decision of the Board of Directors of the Bank, held on 13-1-2003, it was resolved that the judgment-debtor would repay Taka 3 crore in favour of the decree-holder by 31-12-2005 and accordingly, a solenama was filed in Court but the judgment debtor actually re-paid only Taka 90 lac by that date. As such, on the application of the judgment-debtors, the decree-holder bank allowed them time to repay the rest Taka 2 crore 10 lac by 31-12-2008. The judgment-debtors had by that time, re-paid a further amount of Taka 7 lac, as such, both the decree-holder and judgment debtors filed the petition dated 5-6-2006 by way of solenama, that the judgment-debtor would re-pay the rest Taka 2 crore 3 lac in four installments of Taka 50,75,000 by 31-12-2008, without any further interest. The terms and conditions of the said petition was allowed by the Artha Rin Court in Artha Rin Execution Case No. 339 of 2004 and disposed of the execution case upon full satisfaction by its order dated 5-6-2006 (Annexure-B-1). 

 21. On a plain reading of section 38, it would appear that this provision does not envisage filing of any petition of compromise (solenama), rather it envisages final settlement of dispute out of Court, without further claim by the decree-holder from the judgment-debtor. The provision is comparable within Order XXI, rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure. This provision even allows settlement of a dispute on payment of a lesser amount than the decretal dues.
